reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies in the shift from a defense-centric to an attack-centric burden-of-proof paradigm. In the old game, the defense holds the burden until the whistle, implying that the attack must overcome persistent resistance through brute force or coordination. This is modeled as a system where the attack's advancement is constrained by the cumulative interference forces (F_i) and duration (T_p). The battering attack model (A_b) reflects this, where physical engagement determines incremental progress. In contrast, the new game places full burden on the attack, making its success contingent on strategic ingenuity rather than raw force. The defensive strategic resilience (D_s) now becomes the key variable—when attack sophistication (S_a) surpasses defensive strategy effectiveness, the attack succeeds. This creates a dual failure mode: either the attack exhausts itself (as noted in quote 8), or the defense adapts and outwits the attack. The mathematical structure supports a phase transition between these regimes, with equilibrium points defined by the interplay of B_p, A_b, and D_s.
